children: Shares of Acadia Pharmaceuticals were lower after the company said the Phase 3 enabling topline results for its ongoing clinical trial program evaluating remlifanserin for the treatment of hallucinations and delusions associated with Alzheimer's disease psychosis missed its primary endpoint.
The stock was 12% lower, at $22.50, in premarket trade.

For the primary endpoint of change from baseline in the Scale for the Assessment of Positive Symptoms-Hallucinations and Delusions subscales, the change was small for the 60 mg dose. Once-daily 60 mg remlifanserin demonstrated a change of -12.6 versus a -10.4 change for placebo at week 6, yielding a p-value of 0.0603.
The 30 mg dose showed minimal improvement across endpoints compared with placebo.

For the key secondary endpoint, Clinical Global Impression-Severity, the 60 mg dose achieved a change from baseline of -1.3 versus a change of -0.9 for placebo at week 6, yielding a p value of 0.0077. On both efficacy measures, the difference in the 60 mg dose versus placebo increased through the six-week treatment period.

In this study, across both doses, remlifanserin demonstrated a favorable safety profile, with rates of adverse events, serious adverse events, and discontinuations due to adverse events, similar to placebo.

Acadia said it plans to continue enrolling its two ongoing Phase 3 studies evaluating remlifanserin in ADP while implementing amendments to the Phase 3 program, including removing the 30 mg dosage arm.
